rules.name: DEEP SLUMBER
rules.turn:
+slumber-track 0 5, +slumber-track 1 7, +slumber-track 2 8, +slumber-track 3 10
  +slumber-track 4 11, +slumber-track 5 12, +slumber-track 6 13
#acc absorb-uses : spirit @sum
spirit:special S deep-slumber / absorb-uses S 0
absorbed S U / absorb-uses S 1
#acc presence-limit : spirit @sum
absorb-uses S A, slumber-track A M / presence-limit S M
#acc on-island : spirit @sum
presence-of S P, at P L, land L / on-island S 1
#acc under-limit : spirit
on-island S N, presence-limit S M, lt N M / under-limit S
add-presence S, spirit:special S deep-slumber, (presence-choice S C), !(presence-dest S C, under-limit S)
rules.evidence: Spirit Phase growth with 5 on island: no Presence placed; after Absorb Essence (limit 7) slow-phase growth places s6 (l1/l2); serpent-limit 7
rules.notes: The printed track is data (slumber-track index -> limit); the limit is an acc lookup by number of Absorb uses; the narrowing constraint makes the add-presence choice empty when at the limit, and an empty choice resolves to nothing. Purely additive.
rules.text: You start off limited to 5 [Presence] on the island. Raise this with your "Absorb Essence" Power Card. Each use covers the lowest revealed number; your [Presence] limit is the lowest uncovered number. 5 7 8 10 11 12 13

language_issues: A constraint that does not depend on the chosen value (under-limit S) still has to be written inside a `!(...)` that mentions the choice variable (`!(presence-dest S C, under-limit S)`).

core's presence-choice moves every Presence in the supply (`presence-of S P, at P supply` is not a choice), so the scenario keeps one in supply; a real 'add a Presence from your track' needs its own choice.
